GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2020-12-11T09:58:36Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Columns are from different tables while processing dateDiff
Description: I'm trying to calc the next day retention login user with ClickHouse.

The table structure of `t_user_login` is:

```
┌─name────┬─type──────────────────────┬─default_type─┬─default_expression─┬─comment─┬─codec_expression─┬─ttl_expression─┐
│ user    │ String                    │              │                    │         │                  │                │
│ log_day │ DateTime('Asia/Shanghai') │              │                    │         │                  │                │
└─────────┴───────────────────────────┴──────────────┴────────────────────┴─────────┴──────────────────┴────────────────┘
```

And the SQL is:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT log_day,a.user as user_day0,b.user as user_day1
FROM (
  SELECT min(log_day) as log_day, user
  FROM t_user_login
  GROUP BY user
) a
LEFT JOIN t_user_login b
ON dateDiff('day', b.log_day, a.log_day) = 1 AND a.user = b.user;
```

But received an exception:

> Received exception from server (version 20.11.4):
Code: 403. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Invalid columns in JOIN ON section. Columns b.log_day and log_day are from different tables.: While processing dateDiff('day', b.log_day, log_day) = 1.

This really confused me for a long time. Anyone can help me, thanks.

llm_response:

CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about a SQL query syntax problem in ClickHouse where the user is getting an error because of incorrect column references in the JOIN condition. The error message clearly indicates the problem: "Columns b.log_day and log_day are from different tables." The issue is that in the JOIN condition, the user is comparing "b.log_day" with "log_day" (not fully qualified as "a.log_day"). This is purely a SQL syntax issue that can be verified without setting up a build environment. The solution would be to correct the JOIN condition to use fully qualified column names: "ON dateDiff('day', b.log_day, a.log_day) = 1 AND a.user = b.user". This type of issue can be analyzed and verified through code review alone, without needing to run the actual code or set up a ClickHouse environment.
